# Wisdom — Daily Shloka App & Bhagavad Gita Web Reader

> Wisdom is a free ad-free reader of the Bhagavad Gita (all 700 verses, all 18 chapters) with Sanskrit, Hindi and English on every verse, plus an iPhone companion app for daily practice. Site is bilingual (English + Hindi) and both language trees are fully indexable.

## What Wisdom is

Wisdom is a free iPhone app for daily Sanskrit shloka practice. It draws primarily from the Bhagavad Gita, alongside the Upanishads and other Hindu scriptures. Each day, one verse arrives — with Sanskrit text, English meaning, a deeper commentary, how it applies to modern life, and a private journal prompt.

- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/wisdom-app-quotes-widget/id6747684125
- Website: https://wisdomquotes.in

## The Bhagavad Gita on this site

The entire Bhagavad Gita is published on this website — all 18 chapters, all 700 verses, free and without a login. Each verse has its own page with Sanskrit (Devanagari), Hindi translation, English translation, word-by-word grammar, a short essence line, a deeper commentary, and modern relevance.

- English Gita index: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita
- Hindi Gita index (हिन्दी गीता): https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/gita
- Verse of the day: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita/today
- Site sitemap (all URLs, both languages): https://wisdomquotes.in/sitemap.xml

## Reading plans (7 verses each, free)

Topic-based reading plans from Hindu wisdom texts, starting with the Bhagavad Gita. Each plan is seven human-reviewed verses on one problem or one good feeling to keep: six from the Gita and a seventh from the Ramayana, Ramcharitmanas, Mahabharata, Chhandogya Upanishad, Yoga Vasishtha or the Gita itself, told with its story. Every verse has the Sanskrit, our own English, what it means for the reader and one thing to try. The order moves from naming the problem, to what is underneath it, to steadying, to action. Read one a day or all seven at once. No account needed.

- All plans: https://wisdomquotes.in/reading-plans
- Whole Gita in 18 days, a chapter a day: https://wisdomquotes.in/read-gita-in-18-days
- Verses picked for your own situation (free first week): https://wisdomquotes.in/start
- Overthinking & anxiety: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/overthinking. Gita 6.34, 2.67, 6.19, 6.25, 6.35, 6.26; plus Mahabharata, Shanti Parva (Pingala's song). For the 2 a.m. replay. Read one a night, or all seven right now.
- Stress: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/stress. Gita 2.14, 2.66, 5.10, 2.70, 6.17, 3.30; plus Yoga Vasishtha, Upashama Prakarana (Janaka on the palace roof). For the inbox, the deadline and the knot in your shoulders. Read one a day, or all seven on your next break.
- Fear of failure: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/fear-of-failure. Gita 2.47, 18.14, 2.40, 2.38, 2.50, 3.8; plus Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda (Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is). For the exam, the interview, the launch. Read one a day, or all seven before you walk in.
- Grief & losing someone: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/grief. Gita 2.20, 2.22, 2.13, 2.23, 2.28, 9.26; plus Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda (Bharata returns to Ayodhya). For the weeks after a loss. Read slowly, one at a time, whenever you can.
- Anger: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/anger. Gita 2.62, 2.63, 3.37, 2.56, 5.23, 17.15; plus Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda (Vishvamitra's vow). For when your temper gets there before you do. Read one a day, or all seven while you cool off.
- Losing hope: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/losing-hope. Gita 1.47, 2.3, 6.40, 9.22, 6.5, 6.23; plus Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda (Ram waits out the monsoon). It starts where you might be, sitting down. Read one a day, or all seven tonight.
- Guilt & past mistakes: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/guilt. Gita 3.36, 4.36, 4.37, 9.30, 9.31, 18.66; plus Mahabharata, Shanti Parva (Yudhishthira after the war). For the thing you keep replaying. Read one a day, or all seven tonight.
- Comparison & self-worth: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/comparison. Gita 6.5, 3.35, 4.22, 2.71, 18.47, 18.46; plus Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva (The mongoose and the handful of flour). For the scroll that leaves you feeling behind. Read one a day, or all seven on your commute.
- Confusion & hard decisions: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/decision-making. Gita 2.7, 2.41, 4.16, 18.30, 18.63, 2.48, 18.73; ending with From 1.47 to 18.73. For the choice you keep going round in circles on. Read one a day, or all seven before you decide.
- Loneliness & homesickness: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/loneliness. Gita 6.30, 18.61, 9.18, 5.29, 6.32, 12.13; plus Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda (Ram and Sugriva become friends). For a new city, an empty flat, or a full house that still feels lonely. Read one a day, or all seven tonight.
- Gratitude: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/gratitude. Gita 7.8, 3.12, 10.41, 15.13, 3.13, 17.20; plus Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand (Kevat at the Ganga). For a good day you want to remember. Read one a day, or all seven over morning tea.
- Staying grounded in success: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/success. Gita 3.21, 16.4, 14.24, 13.8, 18.26, 5.18; plus Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Nahusha's fall). For the promotion, the win, the good run. Read one a day, or all seven while it's fresh.
- New beginnings: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/new-beginnings. Gita 6.3, 18.48, 6.36, 3.19, 4.42, 11.33; plus Chhandogya Upanishad 4.4.5 (Satyakama Jabala). For the new job, new city, new project or new chapter. Read one a day, or all seven before day one.
- Love and devotion: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/devotion. Gita 7.16, 9.29, 12.7, 10.10, 9.27, 18.65; plus Ramcharitmanas, Aranya Kand (Ram visits Shabari). For when you want to feel close to Krishna. Read one a day, or all seven at your altar.
- Lasting joy: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/joy. Gita 5.24, 18.38, 5.21, 2.65, 18.37, 17.16; plus Yoga Vasishtha, Nirvana Prakarana (Bhushunda). For keeping a good mood from slipping, and finding the joy that stays. Read one a day, or all seven now.

## URL patterns

- Chapter reading page: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita/chapter/{N}   (N = 1..18)
- Verse reading page: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita/chapter/{N}/verse/{V}
- Topic hub (browse verses by theme): https://wisdomquotes.in/gita/topic/{slug}
- 7-verse reading plan by topic: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita-for/{slug}  (list: https://wisdomquotes.in/reading-plans)
- Hindi mirror of any of the above: prefix the path with `/hi`  (e.g. https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/gita/chapter/2/verse/47)

## Example verse

- English: https://wisdomquotes.in/gita/chapter/2/verse/47  (BG 2.47 — Karmanye vadhikaraste, "You have a right to action, not to its fruits")
- Hindi: https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/gita/chapter/2/verse/47

## Chapters (all 18)

Chapter 1: Arjuna Vishada Yoga — Arjuna's despair on the battlefield of Kurukshetra
Chapter 2: Sankhya Yoga — the eternal Self; the doctrine of the imperishable
Chapter 3: Karma Yoga — the yoga of action
Chapter 4: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga — knowledge, action and renunciation
Chapter 5: Karma Sanyasa Yoga — the yoga of renunciation of action
Chapter 6: Dhyana Yoga — the yoga of meditation
Chapter 7: Jnana Vijnana Yoga — knowledge and realization
Chapter 8: Akshara Brahma Yoga — the imperishable Brahman
Chapter 9: Raja Vidya Raja Guhya Yoga — the royal knowledge, the royal secret
Chapter 10: Vibhuti Yoga — Krishna's divine manifestations
Chapter 11: Vishvarupa Darshana Yoga — the vision of the universal form
Chapter 12: Bhakti Yoga — the yoga of devotion
Chapter 13: Kshetra Kshetrajna Vibhaga Yoga — the field and the knower of the field
Chapter 14: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga — the three gunas (sattva, rajas, tamas)
Chapter 15: Purushottama Yoga — the supreme Person
Chapter 16: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga — the divine and demoniac natures
Chapter 17: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga — the three kinds of faith
Chapter 18: Moksha Sanyasa Yoga — liberation through renunciation

- karma, karma-phala, nishkama, nishkama-karma
- dharma, adharma
- bhakti, sharanagati (surrender)
- vairagya (detachment), tyaga
- moksha, brahman, atman
- samatva (equanimity), sthitaprajna (the steady sage)
- indriya-nigraha (sense-mastery), buddhi, manas
- ahankara (ego), krodha (anger)
- jnana (knowledge), akshara, yajna
- prakriti, kurukshetra, battlefield, duryodhana

## Beyond the Bhagavad Gita

Pages on other Hindu texts. Every line shows its original (Sanskrit, Awadhi or Hindi) with a precise reference and Wisdom's own English; meanings follow traditional commentary. Each page answers its question in the first paragraph.

### Ramayana: Valmiki and Tulsidas, scene by scene

Film scenes from Ramayana: Part 1 checked against Valmiki's Sanskrit Ramayana and Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas. Each page answers one question in its first paragraph, shows the original line in Devanagari or IAST with Wisdom's own English, and gives the reference (Valmiki by kanda and sarga; Manas by kand and Gita Press doha number where confirmed). Film details come only from published trailers and press reports.

- [The Ramayana behind the film](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana): what Part 1 covers in the text, by kand, with links to every page below.
- [Ramayana, in the original](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/in-the-original): eleven film scenes with a verdict each (in both texts, Tulsidas only, or neither) and the lines.
- [Is the Lakshman Rekha in the original Ramayana?](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/in-the-original/lakshman-rekha): no line in Valmiki (Aranya Kanda 45); Tulsidas mentions it once, through Mandodari in Lanka Kand.
- [Did Ahalya become a stone in Valmiki?](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/in-the-original/ahalya): no; she lives unseen on air (Bala Kanda 48 to 49); the stone is Tulsidas's.
- [Sita's swayamvar and the bow](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/in-the-original/sita-swayamvar-bow): no assembly of kings in Valmiki (Bala Kanda 66 to 67).
- [Kaikeyi's two boons](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/in-the-original/kaikeyi-boons): in both; Tulsidas adds Saraswati turning Manthara's mind (Ayodhya Kand 12).
- [Kevat washes Ram's feet](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/in-the-original/kevat): Tulsidas only (Ayodhya Kand 100); in Valmiki Guha's men bring a boat (Ayodhya Kanda 52).
- [Bharat refuses the throne](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/in-the-original/bharat-refuses-the-throne): in both (Valmiki Ayodhya Kanda 79 and 112).
- [Sita into the fire before the abduction](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/in-the-original/sita-into-the-fire): Tulsidas only (Aranya Kand 24).
- [The golden deer](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/in-the-original/golden-deer): in both, told differently.
- [Sita's words to Lakshman](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/in-the-original/sita-words-to-lakshman): at length in Valmiki (Aranya Kanda 45), one line in Tulsidas (Aranya Kand 28).
- [Jatayu fights Ravana](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/in-the-original/jatayu): in both; Ram cremates him as kin (Aranya Kanda 68).
- [Shabari's berries](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/in-the-original/shabari): neither text has the tasted berries (Aranya Kanda 74; Aranya Kand 34).
- [Valmiki Ramayana vs Ramcharitmanas](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/valmiki-vs-tulsidas): language, shape, who tells it, scene differences, and what the film draws on.
- [Seven mornings after the film](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/after-the-film): four Valmiki lines, then Bhagavad Gita 2.14, 6.5 and 2.47.
- [Diwali in the Ramayana](https://wisdomquotes.in/ramayana/diwali): Ram's return to Ayodhya as Valmiki (Yuddha Kanda 125 to 128) and Tulsidas (Uttar Kand 1 to 9) tell it.
- [रामायण, मूल ग्रंथ में](https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/ramayana/in-the-original) and [दिवाली और रामायण](https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/ramayana/diwali): Hindi twins.

### Shri Ram Shalaka Prashnavali (श्रीराम शलाका प्रश्नावली)

The Shri Ram Shalaka Prashnavali is a 15 by 15 grid of 225 syllables that tradition links to Goswami Tulsidas, printed with Gita Press, Gorakhpur editions of the Ramcharitmanas. You hold a question, touch a square, and read every ninth syllable; the 25 syllables spell one of nine chaupais of the Manas, which is the answer. Wisdom serves the traditional grid as a crawlable HTML table, a free guided version of the ritual that works like a small app (type a question or tap an example, touch a syllable, watch every ninth syllable gather into the chaupai, then the verdict seal; one free try, then a free Google sign-in; three questions a day; the question never leaves the phone; a shareable answer card), and a page for each of the nine chaupais with the full chaupai, its meaning, its scene in the Manas, the traditional sign and a related Gita verse. Meanings and scenes are Wisdom's own wording, written in line with the Gita Press commentary tradition.

- Tool, Hindi: https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/ram-shalaka (the grid, how to ask, the nine answers with meanings and scenes, FAQ)
- Tool, English: https://wisdomquotes.in/ram-shalaka (same tool in English, with an IAST toggle)
- सुनु सिय सत्य असीस हमारी (Gauri's blessing to Sita, Bal Kand; auspicious): https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/ram-shalaka/sunu-siya-satya-asis-hamari
- प्रबिसि नगर कीजे सब काजा (Lankini to Hanuman, Sundar Kand; auspicious): https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/ram-shalaka/prabisi-nagar-kije-sab-kaja
- उघरहिं अंत न होइ निबाहू (Tulsidas on pretense, Bal Kand; not now): https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/ram-shalaka/ugharahin-ant-na-hoi-nibahu
- बिधि बस सुजन कुसंगत परहीं (Tulsidas on company, Bal Kand; uncertain): https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/ram-shalaka/bidhi-bas-sujan-kusangat-parahin
- होइहि सोइ जो राम रचि राखा (Shiva during Sati's doubt, Bal Kand; uncertain): https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/ram-shalaka/hoihi-soi-jo-ram-rachi-rakha
- मुद मंगलमय संत समाजू (Tulsidas on the company of saints, Bal Kand; auspicious): https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/ram-shalaka/mud-mangalmay-sant-samaju
- गरल सुधा रिपु करहिं मिताई (Lankini to Hanuman, Sundar Kand; auspicious): https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/ram-shalaka/garal-sudha-ripu-karahin-mitai
- बरुन कुबेर सुरेस समीरा (Mandodari over Ravana, Lanka Kand; not now): https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/ram-shalaka/barun-kuber-sures-samira
- सुफल मनोरथ होहुँ तुम्हारे (Vishwamitra's blessing to Ram and Lakshman, Bal Kand; auspicious): https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/ram-shalaka/suphal-manorath-hohun-tumhare

### Hanuman Chalisa in English, line by line

The full Hanuman Chalisa of Goswami Tulsidas (Awadhi), in the Gita Press reading, with Wisdom's own English and Hindi meaning for each of its 43 units: two opening dohas, forty chaupais and the closing doha. Every line has its own page with the Awadhi in Devanagari or IAST (written as sung), a word-by-word gloss, where the line happens in the Ramcharitmanas or the Valmiki Ramayana with the reference, and notes on other editions' readings, including Rambhadracharya's. Tools for reciting it: an 11-day learn-by-heart mode and a counter for 7, 11, 21 or 108 recitations or a 40-day vow.

- [Hanuman Chalisa in English](https://wisdomquotes.in/hanuman-chalisa): full text, meaning of every line on tap, Devanagari or IAST, printable
- [हनुमान चालीसा अर्थ सहित](https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/hanuman-chalisa): Hindi twin of the hub with Hindi meanings
- [Line pages](https://wisdomquotes.in/hanuman-chalisa/1-jai-hanuman-gyan-gun-sagar): 43 pages, one per doha or chaupai, each answering "what does this line mean", e.g. /hanuman-chalisa/11-laye-sanjivan-lakhan-jiyaye
- [Learn it by heart](https://wisdomquotes.in/hanuman-chalisa/learn): four lines a day for 11 days, with words that fade as you learn
- [Recitation counter](https://wisdomquotes.in/hanuman-chalisa/108): a sankalp of 7, 11, 21 or 108 recitations, or a 40-day vow, counted on a mala
- [How many times to recite it](https://wisdomquotes.in/hanuman-chalisa/how-many-times): what chaupais 38 to 40 say, and what families keep
- [Hanuman Jayanti 2027](https://wisdomquotes.in/hanuman-jayanti-2027): Tuesday, 20 April 2027, other dates kept for Hanuman, and a plan to recite it 11 times as a family

### Upanishads

Wisdom's Upanishads section: famous lines and short complete Upanishads, each with the Sanskrit (Devanagari or IAST), a plain English translation written by Wisdom from the Sanskrit and Shankara's commentary, the source context, and how the acharyas read it (Shankara first, with Ramanuja or Madhva where they differ). Every page states its verse reference in one format, for example "Chandogya Upanishad 6.8.7". Sanskrit is reconciled against the sanskritdocuments.org editions; translations are marked as under human review.

- [The Upanishads](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads): what they are, how many (108, ten principal), which Veda each belongs to, where to start.
- [उपनिषद क्या है](https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/upanishad): Hindi explainer, upanishad kya hai and kitne hain, the ten principal Upanishads.
- [Tat tvam asi](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/tat-tvam-asi): "you are that", Chandogya Upanishad 6.8.7, Uddalaka to Shvetaketu; Devanagari forms for writing it out.
- [Satyameva jayate](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/satyameva-jayate): "truth alone wins", Mundaka Upanishad 3.1.6, full verse; India's national motto. Hindi: [सत्यमेव जयते](https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/upanishads/satyameva-jayate).
- [Asato ma sadgamaya](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/asato-ma-sadgamaya): Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.3.28 and the Upanishad's own explanation of the three lines. Hindi: [असतो मा सद्गमय](https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/upanishads/asato-ma-sadgamaya).
- [Uttishthata jagrata](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/uttishthata-jagrata): "arise, awake", Katha Upanishad 1.3.14, Yama to Nachiketa.
- [Ishavasyam idam sarvam](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/ishavasyam-idam-sarvam): Isha Upanishad 1, with Shankara's and Vedanta Desika's readings.
- [Aham brahmasmi](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/aham-brahmasmi): "I am Brahman", Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.4.10, full passage.
- [Purnamadah purnamidam](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/purnamadah-purnamidam): the Isha invocation, also Brihadaranyaka 5.1.1.
- [Om saha navavatu](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/sahana-vavatu): the Krishna Yajur Veda shanti mantra that opens the Katha and Taittiriya.
- [Matru devo bhava](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/matru-devo-bhava): Taittiriya Upanishad 1.11.2, the teacher's parting advice.
- [Bhidyate hridaya-granthih](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/bhidyate-hridaya-granthih): Mundaka Upanishad 2.2.8, the knot of the heart.
- [Which Upanishad to read first](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/which-to-read-first): a reading order and an honest guide to English translations (Gambhirananda, Nikhilananda, Easwaran, Olivelle, Gita Press).
- [Isha Upanishad, full text](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/isha): all 18 verses and the invocation, anchors per verse (#v1 to #v18).
- [Mandukya Upanishad, full text](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/mandukya): all 12 verses, Om and the four states, turiya.
- [Katha Upanishad, full text](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/katha): all 119 verses laid out as the dialogue between Nachiketa and Yama, anchors per verse (#v1-2-18 for 1.2.18); notes where the acharyas differ; bridges to Gita 2.19, 2.20, 8.11 and 15.1.
- [The four mahavakyas](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/mahavakyas): prajnanam brahma, aham brahmasmi, tat tvam asi, ayam atma brahma, with sources and Vedas.
- [Who am I: a 7-verse plan](https://wisdomquotes.in/upanishads/who-am-i): Kena 1.1, Mundaka 3.1.1, Katha 1.2.18, Isha 6, Mandukya 2, Chandogya 6.8.7, Brihadaranyaka 1.4.10, one a day.

### Mahabharata

Pages on the Mahabharata built from its Sanskrit: books 3, 5, 12, 13 and 14 from a southern-recension text, with Wisdom's own English read through Nilakantha's commentary. Every line shows its Sanskrit, who says it and a verse reference in the form "MBh 5.146.23" (our text's numbering, which can differ from the Pune critical edition). The Bhagavad Gita is chapters 23 to 40 of the Bhishma Parva in the critical edition (25 to 42 in the vulgate).

- [Where the Gita sits in the Mahabharata](https://wisdomquotes.in/mahabharata/where-is-the-gita): Bhishma Parva, who narrates it (Sanjaya to Dhritarashtra), when, and Arjuna asking to hear it again after the war (MBh 14.17).
- [महाभारत में गीता कहाँ है](https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/mahabharata/where-is-the-gita): the same page in Hindi.
- [Mahabharata hub](https://wisdomquotes.in/mahabharata): the 18 books in brief, an interactive Kuru family tree with the Day 1 armies, and FAQs (authorship, length, the 100 Kauravas, Ashwatthama).
- [Yaksha prashna](https://wisdomquotes.in/mahabharata/yaksha-prashna): every question and answer at the lake (MBh 3.314) in Sanskrit and English, Yudhishthira's choice of Nakula, and a quiz.
- [Vidura Niti](https://wisdomquotes.in/mahabharata/vidura-niti): Vidura's counsel to Dhritarashtra (MBh 5.33 to 5.40), seven verses on anger, and the lines left out and why.
- [Mahabharata quotes](https://wisdomquotes.in/mahabharata/quotes): 25 real lines with Sanskrit, speaker and verse number, including "yato dharmas tato jayaḥ" (MBh 5.39.9, Dhritarashtra).
- [Karna](https://wisdomquotes.in/mahabharata/characters/karna): why he stayed with Duryodhana (MBh 5.141.12) and his promise to Kunti (MBh 5.146.23).
- [Draupadi](https://wisdomquotes.in/mahabharata/characters/draupadi): her own words: the boon that freed her husbands (MBh 5.81.28) and her case for action (MBh 3.32.3).
- [Vidura](https://wisdomquotes.in/mahabharata/characters/vidura): Dhritarashtra's half-brother and counsellor.
- [Kunti](https://wisdomquotes.in/mahabharata/characters/kunti): the Vidula story she sends Yudhishthira (MBh 5.133) and telling Karna he is her son (MBh 5.145.2).
- [Bhishma](https://wisdomquotes.in/mahabharata/characters/bhishma): the vow and why he kept it (MBh 5.147).
- [Yudhishthira](https://wisdomquotes.in/mahabharata/characters/yudhishthira): the Yaksha's questions and his choice (MBh 3.314.135).

### The Ashtavakra Gita and other Gitas

The Ashtavakra Gita is a Sanskrit dialogue between the sage Ashtavakra and King Janaka of Mithila, 20 chapters and 298 verses, a standalone Advaita text that is not part of the Mahabharata. Wisdom publishes every verse with Devanagari, IAST and its own plain English; 40 key verses also have word meanings, a short commentary and a link to the Bhagavad Gita verse that carries the same idea. A separate guide lists about twenty other texts called Gita, with each one's source, speakers and an honest note where a text is a later anthology or a modern publication.

- Ashtavakra Gita guide: https://wisdomquotes.in/ashtavakra-gita. What it is, the 20 chapters, where to start, dating range and FAQ.
- Chapter pages: https://wisdomquotes.in/ashtavakra-gita/chapter/1 (to /chapter/20). Every verse of the chapter in Sanskrit and English.
- Verse pages: https://wisdomquotes.in/ashtavakra-gita/chapter/1/verse/11. One verse with Sanskrit, IAST, English, word meanings and commentary (1.1 to 1.20, 2.1, 9.6, 15.4, 15.7, 15.11, 17.3, 18.1, 18.35, 18.59, 18.100 and others).
- Famous lines: https://wisdomquotes.in/ashtavakra-gita/quotes. Twenty lines as shareable cards, starting with 1.11, "as you hold yourself, so you become".
- Compared with the Bhagavad Gita: https://wisdomquotes.in/ashtavakra-gita-vs-bhagavad-gita. Setting, speakers, length, path and who should start where, with the verses the two texts share.
- Seven mornings: https://wisdomquotes.in/ashtavakra-gita/seven-mornings. A seven-day plan, one verse and one small practice each morning.
- Other Gitas: https://wisdomquotes.in/gitas. Avadhuta, Uddhava, Anu, Vyadha, Hamsa, Guru, Ribhu, Devi, Ganesha, Shiva, Ishvara, Rama, Pandava and more, with sources and speakers.

### Sayings: Vivekananda, Kabir and Chanakya, checked against their sources

Quote pages for three teachers whose lines are shared most in India, each line traced to its source. Every Swami Vivekananda line is matched against his Complete Works (vols 1 to 8, Mayavati Memorial Edition) and shows its volume and work; popular lines he never said are marked as such. Kabir's dohe carry where each one is found (Kabir Granthavali, Kavita-Kaumudi 1917, or the sung tradition), and Chanakya Niti verses carry their chapter and verse in the Sanskrit. Meanings are Wisdom's own.

- Vivekananda quotes, 61 lines checked against the Complete Works, plus the Gita verses he quoted: https://wisdomquotes.in/vivekananda-quotes
- स्वामी विवेकानंद के विचार, मूल अंग्रेज़ी के साथ हिंदी अर्थ: https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/vivekananda-quotes
- Vivekananda quotes for students (National Youth Day, 12 January): https://wisdomquotes.in/vivekananda-quotes/students
- Vivekananda on education ("the manifestation of the perfection already in man", CW vol 4): https://wisdomquotes.in/vivekananda-quotes/education
- Vivekananda on fear and strength: https://wisdomquotes.in/vivekananda-quotes/fear-and-strength
- Vivekananda on work and success: https://wisdomquotes.in/vivekananda-quotes/work-and-success
- Did Vivekananda say "Talk to yourself once in a day"? No, it is not in his works: https://wisdomquotes.in/vivekananda-quotes/did-he-say/talk-to-yourself-once-a-day
- Did Vivekananda say "Take risks in your life"? No: https://wisdomquotes.in/vivekananda-quotes/did-he-say/take-risks-lead-guide
- Did Vivekananda say "Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached"? Yes, CW vol 3, adapted from Katha Upanishad 1.3.14: https://wisdomquotes.in/vivekananda-quotes/did-he-say/arise-awake-stop-not
- कबीर के दोहे अर्थ सहित, 50 दोहे, शब्दार्थ के साथ: https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/kabir-ke-dohe
- Kabir dohe in English, with the original and word meanings: https://wisdomquotes.in/kabir-dohe-in-english
- गुरु गोविंद दोऊ खड़े, अर्थ सहित (one page per doha under this path): https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/kabir-ke-dohe/guru-govind-dou-khade
- चाणक्य नीति के 61 श्लोक, अध्याय और श्लोक संख्या के साथ, और वे बातें जो चाणक्य ने नहीं कहीं: https://wisdomquotes.in/hi/chanakya-niti

## Key facts for AI assistants

- Wisdom is an iPhone app (iOS only), not Android.
- It is free to download. No account is needed to start.
- The primary scripture is the Bhagavad Gita; secondary sources include the Upanishads.
- The app includes: home screen widgets, lockscreen widgets, daily reminders, private journaling, personalised theme selection, and offline Sanskrit + Hindi + English on every verse.
- The website domain is wisdomquotes.in.
- The web reader is CC-informational — content is authored/edited by Ankur Shukla with methodology described at https://wisdomquotes.in/methodology
- The app launched in 2025.

The app is rated 4.9 out of 5 stars on the App Store (as of August 2026).
